AUC(t) Competing Risks Measure

Source: R/MeasureCompRisksAUC.R
mlr_measures_cmprsk.auc.Rd

Calculates the time-dependent ROC-AUC at a specific time point, as described in Blanche et al. (2013), Equation 4. Controls include subjects who survive beyond the time horizon and those who experience a competing event before the horizon.

Details

By default, this measure returns a cause-independent AUC(t) score, calculated as a weighted average of the cause-specific AUCs. The weights correspond to the relative event frequencies of each cause, following Equation 7 in Heyard et al. (2020). User-supplied weights are also supported through cause_weights. See the Cause weights section for weighting rules.

Alternatively, users can obtain the cause-specific AUC(t) for any individual cause by specifying the cause parameter.

Calls riskRegression::Score() with:

  • metric = "auc"

  • cens.method = "ipcw"

  • cens.model = "km"

Notes on the riskRegression implementation:

  1. IPCW weights are estimated using the test data only, so smaller test sets may lead to less stable estimates.

  2. Scoring at a time beyond the maximum observed test-set time produces an input error.

  3. AUC(t) is undefined if no events of the requested cause are observed at or before time, or if no controls are available at that time. In these cases, riskRegression returns NaN for the cause-specific AUC.

Dictionary

This Measure can be instantiated via the dictionary mlr_measures or with the associated sugar function msr():

mlr_measures$get("cmprsk.auc")
msr("cmprsk.auc")

Cause weights

Cause weights are used only for cause = "mean". The cause_weights parameter is ignored when scoring a specific cause.

With cause_weights = NULL, weights are the relative frequencies of observed non-censored events from the test set. Causes without observed events receive zero weight, are listed in a warning and are skipped when calculating the mean score. If no events from any cause are observed, weights are undefined, and the measure warns and returns NA_real_.

Alternatively, the user can supply custom weights via cause_weights. Weights must be finite, non-negative, sum to 1, and contain one entry per predicted cause. Entries must match the order of the predicted CIFs cause names. If any user-supplied weight happens to be zero, it is skipped silently.

In general, non-finite scores from positive-weight causes propagate to the mean, causing the measure to return NaN and a warning identifies the causes with non-finite scores.

Parameter details

  • cause (numeric(1)|"mean")
    Integer number indicating which cause to use. Default value is "mean" which returns an event-frequency weighted mean of the cause-specific AUCs.

  • cause_weights (numeric()|NULL)
    Optional custom weights for cause = "mean". See the Cause weights section for weighting rules.

  • time (numeric(1))
    Single time point at which to return the score. If NULL, the median observed time point from the test set is used.

References

Blanche, Paul, Dartigues, Francois J, Jacqmin-Gadda, Helene (2013). “Estimating and comparing time-dependent areas under receiver operating characteristic curves for censored event times with competing risks.” Statistics in Medicine, 32(30), 5381–5397. ISSN 1097-0258, doi:10.1002/SIM.5958 , https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/sim.5958.

Spitoni, Claudia, Lammens, Valerie, Putter, Hein (2018). “Prediction errors for state occupation and transition probabilities in multi-state models.” Biometrical Journal, 60(1), 34–48. ISSN 0323-3847, doi:10.1002/BIMJ.201600191 , https://doi.org/10.1002/BIMJ.201600191.

Heyard, Rachel, Timsit, Jean-Francois, Held, Leonhard (2020). “Validation of discrete time-to-event prediction models in the presence of competing risks.” Biometrical Journal, 62(3), 643–657. https://doi.org/10.1002/BIMJ.201800293.

Examples

# Define a task
task = tsk("pbc")
task$select(c("age", "chol", "albumin", "ast", "bili", "protime"))

# Stratify by event status
task$set_col_roles(cols = "status", add_to = "stratum")
task
#> 
#> ── <TaskCompRisks> (276x8): Primary Biliary Cholangitis ────────────────────────
#> • Target: time and status
#> • Properties: strata
#> • Features (6):
#>   • dbl (4): albumin, ast, bili, protime
#>   • int (2): age, chol
#> • Strata: status

# Create training and test sets
set.seed(42L)
part = partition(task)

# Define the learner
learner = lrn("cmprsk.fg")

# Train on the training set
learner$train(task, row_ids = part$train)
learner$native_model
#> $`1`
#> convergence:  TRUE 
#> coefficients:
#>        age    albumin        ast       bili       chol    protime 
#> -0.0977200 -0.3992000 -0.0019480  0.0006162  0.0009104 -0.2221000 
#> standard errors:
#> [1] 0.027980 0.924300 0.003838 0.076710 0.001232 0.393500
#> two-sided p-values:
#>     age albumin     ast    bili    chol protime 
#> 0.00048 0.67000 0.61000 0.99000 0.46000 0.57000 
#> 
#> $`2`
#> convergence:  TRUE 
#> coefficients:
#>        age    albumin        ast       bili       chol    protime 
#>  4.543e-02 -1.020e+00  3.061e-03  1.200e-01  6.019e-05  2.155e-01 
#> standard errors:
#> [1] 0.0132100 0.2377000 0.0019090 0.0173200 0.0003912 0.1083000
#> two-sided p-values:
#>     age albumin     ast    bili    chol protime 
#> 5.8e-04 1.8e-05 1.1e-01 4.3e-12 8.8e-01 4.7e-02 
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "fine_gray"

# Predict CIFs for the test set
predictions = learner$predict(task, row_ids = part$test)
predictions
#> 
#> ── <PredictionCompRisks> for 92 observations: ──────────────────────────────────
#>  row_ids time event       CIF
#>        1   13     2 <list[2]>
#>       10  123     2 <list[2]>
#>       16    4     2 <list[2]>
#>      ---  ---   ---       ---
#>      157   73     1 <list[2]>
#>      208   27     1 <list[2]>
#>      213   47     1 <list[2]>

# AUC at the median observed test-set time,
# weighted by event frequencies
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc"))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>  0.8691053 

# AUC at 100 months, weighted by event frequencies
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc", time = 100))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>  0.8279221 

# AUC at 100 months, with equal weights for both causes
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc", time = 100, cause_weights = c(0.5, 0.5)))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>  0.8219801 

# AUC at 100 months, with custom weights for transplant and death
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc", time = 100, cause_weights = c(0.2, 0.8)))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>  0.8269254 

# AUC at 100 months, for transplant only
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc", time = 100, cause = 1))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>   0.813738 

# AUC at 100 months, for death only
predictions$score(msr("cmprsk.auc", time = 100, cause = 2))
#> cmprsk.auc 
#>  0.8302222
